facts.raw_span: A 34-year-old woman
gravida 2 para 1
previous cesarean section
presented at 4 weeks 5 days of amenorrhea
1-day history of epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen
denied fever, nausea, vomiting, or vaginal bleeding
afebrile, hemodynamically stable
epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs were negative
white blood cell count of 13.54×10^9/L
β-hCG level of 523 IU/L
empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness

concepts.why: The patient presents with amenorrhea, epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, and a β-hCG level below the discriminatory zone, with an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound, suggesting an ectopic pregnancy.
The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain, tenderness, and elevated white blood cell count could be indicative of pelvic inflammatory disease.
The patient's ultrasound showing a left adnexal structure could be indicative of an ovarian cyst.
The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen and elevated white blood cell count could be indicative of appendicitis.
The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain and elevated white blood cell count could be indicative of gastroenteritis.
The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain and elevated white blood cell count could be indicative of diverticulitis.
The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain and elevated white blood cell count could be indicative of a urinary tract infection.
The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain and elevated white blood cell count could be indicative of salpingitis.

rationales.F04: Early presentation of amenorrhea increases the likelihood of ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F05: Epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen is a common symptom of ectopic pregnancy and other gynecological conditions.
rationales.F09: Negative Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs decrease the likelihood of appendicitis.
rationales.F11: The β-hCG level is below the discriminatory zone, which increases the likelihood of ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F12: An empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness on ultrasound is highly suggestive of ectopic pregnancy.
